recognize_zh: 鼻腔抹片中可見兩個上皮細胞，細胞質淡藍、蒼白略呈泡沫狀，圓核偏向一側；但杯狀（cup-like）外形與分泌黏液在此圖中不明顯，辨識需搭配檢體來源。
features: Isolated epithelial cells with moderate amounts of pale blue, faintly vacuolated (foamy) cytoplasm
Single round nucleus with speckled, finely granular chromatin, eccentrically placed in the right cell
Distinct goblet (cup/chalice) shape and apical mucin vacuole not clearly appreciable
Mucoid, finely granular pink-purple background with debris
Refractile brown particle next to the left cell, likely exogenous debris
Image focus and resolution are limited
describe_en: Nasal smear stained with a Romanowsky-type stain shows scattered epithelial cells in a mucoid, granular background. The cells have a single round nucleus with speckled chromatin and pale, faintly foamy blue cytoplasm; in one cell the nucleus is displaced toward one pole. A classic chalice shape with a distended apical mucin vacuole is not clearly demonstrated at this resolution. Findings are compatible with, but not diagnostic of, goblet cells of respiratory mucosa.

ddx.vs: Ciliated cells are columnar with a terminal plate and apical cilia rather than a mucin-distended foamy cytoplasm.
Squamous cells are larger and flat with abundant homogeneous angular cytoplasm and a small central nucleus, without foamy mucin.
Macrophages have a bean-shaped or folded nucleus and vacuoles containing phagocytosed debris rather than a single basal round nucleus under a mucin cup.
